```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has <- function(...) all(vapply(c(...), requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))
```

Bank and insurance data rarely fits in a data frame. credgate works on
**Arrow** tables and **Parquet** files, and on tables in **DuckDB** and other
databases through DBI and dbplyr, reading them in chunks so the data may be
larger than memory. The packages are optional: install the ones you use.

All data in this vignette is synthetic.

```{r}
library(credgate)

recs <- synth_indian_pii(2000, seed = 42)
templates <- c(
  "Shri %s called about a failed UPI payment to %s.",
  "Name: %s. PAN %s verified; wants the EMI date moved.",
  "Branch hours query, no customer details given."
)
n <- 20000
i <- (seq_len(n) - 1) %% nrow(recs) + 1
kind <- seq_len(n) %% 3 + 1
calls <- data.frame(
  call_id = seq_len(n),
  cust_pan = recs$pan[i],
  mobile = as.numeric(recs$mobile[i]),
  amount = round(seq_len(n) * 7.31 %% 250000, 2),
  notes = ifelse(kind == 1, sprintf(templates[1], recs$name[i], recs$upi_id[i]),
    ifelse(kind == 2, sprintf(templates[2], recs$name[i], recs$pan[i]), templates[3])
  )
)
```

## Which columns hold personal data?

`scan_pii()` takes a data frame, an Arrow `Table` or `Dataset`, or a database
table from dbplyr. Arrow and database tables are read **one column at a
time, in chunks**, and sampled exactly as in memory: the report is the same
whatever the size of the table.

```{r}
scan_pii(calls, sample = 5000)
```

## Arrow and Parquet

```{r, eval = has("arrow")}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
arrow::write_parquet(calls, path, chunk_size = 5000)

# Scan the file without loading it:
scan_pii(arrow::open_dataset(path), sample = 5000)
```

`redact_parquet()` writes a redacted copy, `batch_size` rows at a time.
Columns you do not name are copied unchanged, so drop or tokenise the
structured identifier columns separately:

```{r, eval = has("arrow")}
safe <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
redact_parquet(path, safe, columns = "notes", min_confidence = 0.5)
head(arrow::read_parquet(safe, col_select = c("call_id", "notes")), 3)
```

`redact()`, `tokenise()` and `detect_pii()` also accept Arrow arrays and
return an Arrow array:

```{r, eval = has("arrow")}
redact(arrow::Array$create(c("PAN ABCPE1234F", NA, "no PII")))
```

## DuckDB and other databases

With dbplyr, `scan_pii()` works on any database table: DuckDB, Postgres,
SQLite, and others with a DBI driver. The query is run once per column, in
chunks.

```{r, eval = has("duckdb", "DBI", "dbplyr", "dplyr")}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "calls", calls)

scan_pii(dplyr::tbl(con, "calls"), sample = 5000)

# Any dbplyr query works, not only whole tables:
recent <- dplyr::filter(dplyr::tbl(con, "calls"), call_id > 15000)
scan_pii(recent, sample = 1000)
```

DuckDB cannot call R functions from SQL, so `redact_query()` fetches a
query's result in chunks, redacts the text columns and appends them to a new
table. With DuckDB the query can read files directly, and `COPY` writes the
result back to Parquet:

```{r, eval = has("duckdb", "DBI")}
redact_query(con, "SELECT call_id, amount, notes FROM calls", "calls_safe",
  min_confidence = 0.5
)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM calls_safe LIMIT 3")

out <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
DBI::dbExecute(con, sprintf("COPY calls_safe TO '%s' (FORMAT parquet)", out))
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

For a Parquet file, `redact_query(con, "SELECT * FROM 'calls.parquet'", ...)`
reads it without loading it into R first.

### Other databases

Any database with a DBI driver works the same way: `redact_query()` needs
only DBI, and `scan_pii()` takes a dbplyr table. For example, Postgres:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "lending", host = "db.internal")
scan_pii(dplyr::tbl(con, "loan_notes"))                     # needs dbplyr
redact_query(con, "SELECT id, notes FROM loan_notes", "loan_notes_safe")
```

credgate is tested with DuckDB, SQLite and Postgres. `scan_pii()` reads each
column twice (to count, then to sample), so its sample matches the in-memory
one only if the database returns rows in the same order both times, as these
do for plain tables. Postgres and SQLite cannot write on a connection while
a query is open on it, so with one connection `redact_query()` keeps the
redacted chunks in temporary files until the query has been read, then
writes them in one transaction; pass a second connection as `to_con` to
write as it reads.

## Sizes and speed

credgate processes roughly 0.2-0.3 MB of text per second per core in R (see
the throughput section of the repository's `benchmark/README.md`). For very
large tables, scan first: structured columns such as `cust_pan` are better
dropped or tokenised as whole columns, leaving detection for free-text
columns only.
